history.dynasty: Jat rulers of Bharatpur; Maharaja Balwant Singh
history.period: Mid-19th century; construction begun 1845, reportedly completed after about nine decades (per tourmyindia - verify)
history.summary: The Ganga Mandir stands in the heart of Bharatpur city near Lohagarh Fort. Maharaja Balwant Singh began construction in 1845; funding was unusual - state employees and affluent residents were asked to donate a month's pay - and the work reportedly took about nine decades. Balwant Singh's fifth descendant, Brijendra Singh, later installed the white-marble idol of Goddess Ganga seated on a crocodile, giving the temple its name. The two-storey red-sandstone structure blends Rajput, Mughal and South Indian styles with elaborate carvings on pillars and panels (one source likens its look to a French neo-classical chateau). Noted features: a gong audible from a distance, a four-foot idol of King Bhagirath, and entrance sculptures of Krishna lifting Govardhan alongside Shiva-Parvati and Lakshmi-Narayan; a window of the royal palace is said to face the sanctum for the royal family's darshan (verify). name: Ganga Mandir
town_description: Bharatpur is a city in eastern Rajasthan, the former capital of the Jat kingdom of the same name, famous for the Lohagarh Fort and the Keoladeo National Park. The Ganga Mandir sits in the city centre near Mathura Gate and Pai Bagh, close to the fort.
